limits: Matches prove client input bytes and archive/manifest binding; they do not directly inspect server image-decoder internals. Repair-request aliases duplicate one recorded request each.

visual_review.initial_head: Panel and target button fully framed; gripper ends cropped at lower edge.
visual_review.last_head: Panel/button and both grippers visible. The white marker on the right gripper is seen edge-on as a narrow light strip, not the conspicuous arrow shape of the wrist view; exact marked physical tip identity remains less clear.
visual_review.last_wrist: Button upper-left, clear large white arrow on the right finger. Only head commands explain near-constant wrist framing.

timing_interpretation: All head frames were received after send completion. Capture uses an early post-send observation rather than measured arrival. Next-movement start samples 47–65 seconds later still show prior head target not reached, so evidence does not support attributing all target errors solely to a short image-capture delay. Cause requires controller/hold-path inspection.
